title: Fifty, and Never Headed
title_candidates: Kent Bites Back — Except at Baker
The Best Gross Ever, on Courses Nobody Knew
theme: Four brand-new Kent links, four days of collective punishment — and one man who read them like a local. Jon Baker's +50 is the best gross aggregate in TEG history, posted while the rest of the field filled the card with 8s and 9s.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck register: affectionate ribbing anchored to real numbers
opening_hook: Open on Littlestone in R3, the single most extraordinary day of scoring in TEG memory — Jon Baker's +8 gross (2nd-best gross round ever, b05) and John Patterson's 49 points (3rd-best round ever, b06) on the same marsh on the same afternoon — then loop back to Deal to explain how a tournament producing numbers like that was never actually in doubt.
foreshadow: Jon Baker arrives on back-to-back Jacket wins and nobody in the field has ever seen any of these four courses — no course records exist to aim at, so he simply invents one.
David Mullin arrives as reigning Wooden Spoon holder with back-to-back Spoons and eight prior Jacket wins: the most decorated gross golfer in TEG history, currently in freefall.
John Patterson, defending Trophy champion, signs for an 8 at Royal Cinque Ports' 1st hole and is last in the Spoon race by the 2nd — the carnage and the brilliance are the same man.
Gregg Williams comes in with three prior Trophy wins and Jacket 3rd in each of the last three TEGs — and is the only man all TEG to get his hands on the lead.

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.how: Baker led from R1 H2 and was in front at every round's end (39-36-44-39 = 158). The only genuine pressure came at Prince's in R2: after 32 straight holes in front he was overhauled by Gregg Williams at the 16th (b01), then reclaimed the outright lead two holes later with a birdie at the 18th (b33) — the decisive takeover. Williams drew level again at R3 H1 (b43), whereupon Baker's 44 points at Littlestone (b05, b12) opened five, and R4's 39 closed it out by six (b03). No lead change was ever recorded in the final round.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.how: Wire-to-wire and never troubled: 85 at Royal Cinque Ports gave him a nine-shot cushion on day one, 88 at Prince's held seven, then +8 at Littlestone (79 gross, b05 — second-best gross round in TEG history) blew it out to fourteen, and 85 in R4 finished the job by eighteen from Williams. The aggregate +50 (b02) is the best gross total in TEG history, and his third Jacket in succession.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: For three rounds the Spoon looked like Patterson's (bottom after R1 and R2) or Alex Baker's (bottom after R3, b18). Mullin's own slide was quiet and continuous — 3rd, 3rd, 4th — until R4 at Prince's Shore, where a 9 at the par-4 10th (SI 3; b14) dropped him to last for the first time all tournament (b10) with eight holes to play, and he never got back out. 135 points (b11): a third consecutive Spoon and a fourth in all, for the man with eight Green Jackets on the shelf.

headline_candidates: Deal or No Deal: Baker Nine Clear, Patterson Signs for 108
The Wind, the Links, and Four Trips Past Eight
rounds.chosen_headline: Deal or No Deal: Baker Nine Clear, Patterson Signs for 108
rounds.angle: TEG's first ball in Kent is struck on an Open championship links and the scoreboard immediately splits in two: Baker 85 and 39 points, everyone else clinging on — Patterson's 108 built on an 8 at the 1st, a 9 at the 7th and a 9 at the 16th.

headline_candidates: Thirty-Two Holes in Front, Two Holes Behind
rounds.angle: The only real contest of the tournament: Williams finally prises the Trophy lead away after Baker's 32-hole tenure (b01), and gets to keep it for two holes before a birdie at the last hands it straight back (b33).

headline_candidates: Littlestone, Little Resistance: 44 and 49 on the Marsh
Two of the Best Rounds in TEG History, One Afternoon
Patterson Finds Everything Except a Leaderboard
rounds.chosen_headline: Littlestone, Little Resistance: 44 and 49 on the Marsh
rounds.angle: The scoring day of the TEG and arguably of TEG history — Baker's +8 (b05) and 44 points, Patterson's 49 points and personal-best +12 (b06, b07) — while at the other end of the field Alex Baker's 8 at the 2nd (b28) leaves him bottom of the Spoon race (b18).

headline_candidates: Shore Thing: Baker Doubles Up, Mullin Spoons at the 10th
Fifty: A Number Nobody Has Ever Posted
Eight Jackets, Three Spoons: Mullin's 9 at the Tenth
rounds.chosen_headline: Shore Thing: Baker Doubles Up, Mullin Spoons at the 10th
rounds.angle: Baker signs for 85 to complete the record +50 and the Trophy-Jacket double (b02, b03); Patterson makes the TEG's only eagle at the par-5 2nd (b04, b15) and then a 9 at the 15th (b30); Alex Baker posts a personal-best +17 (b08); and Mullin's 9 at the 10th (b14) settles the Spoon (b10, b11).

players.arc: Arrives on back-to-back Jackets and leaves with a third, the best gross aggregate in TEG history (+50), the Trophy by six, and a solitary two-hole wobble at Prince's 16th as the only blemish on four days in front.

Three prior Trophy wins and third in the Jacket for three TEGs running; here he was the only man to touch the lead (R2 H16, R3 H1) and the reward was to finish second in both the Trophy and the Jacket — a promotion, of a sort.

The defending Trophy champion produced the tournament's worst round (108 at Deal), its third-best round in TEG history (49 at Littlestone), its only eagle, a personal-best gross, and seven separate trips to quadruple bogey or worse — golf as weather system rather than performance.
Eight-time Green Jacket winner and reigning Spoon holder, he slid 3rd-3rd-4th-5th and made it official with a 9 at Prince's 10th: a third consecutive Wooden Spoon, and a fourth in total.

A former Trophy winner who spent R1 and R3 bleeding shots in clusters and briefly held bottom place, then salvaged real credit at Prince's Shore with a personal-best +17 — and let his brother clean up everything else.

venue_notes: TEG's first visit to Kent, England (2020) and four courses none of the field had ever played — every round is a first visit for every player, so there is no course history to lean on and no prior records to break. Open with Royal Cinque Ports at Deal (championship links, two Open Championships, brutal in wind) as the explanation for R1's gross numbers; Prince's at Sandwich appears twice in different configurations (Dunes/Himalayas in R2, the stronger Shore/Dunes routing in R4), which is worth a line as a returning stage rather than a repeat course; Littlestone on the Romney Marshes, laid out by the architect of Royal St George's and refined by Braid and MacKenzie, is the natural setting for the R3 scoring explosion — the remote, unglamorous one that gave up the two best rounds of the tournament.
course_history_notes: Every player, every course: first visit. No prior gross to beat anywhere in Kent, so this TEG sets all four baselines.
Baseline highs and lows: Jon Baker's 79 at Littlestone is the lowest gross of the tournament; Patterson's 108 at Royal Cinque Ports the highest.
Littlestone gave up the field's best numbers of the tournament — Jon Baker 79, Patterson 83, Williams 86 — on the day it mattered most to the Trophy.
Prince's Shore/Dunes in R4 produced Alex Baker's best round of the tournament (89 gross, a personal best at +17) and Mullin's Spoon-sealing 9.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R2 H18 at Prince's — Baker birdies the last to take back the outright lead he had lost two holes earlier (b33, b01), and is never headed across the final 36 holes.
Green Jacket: R3 at Littlestone — +8 gross (79, b05) stretches a seven-shot cushion to fourteen and turns the Jacket into a formality en route to the record +50 (b02).
Wooden Spoon: R4 H10 at Prince's Shore — Mullin's 9 at the par-4 SI 3 (b14) drops him to last for the first time all tournament (b10) with eight holes left.

payoffs.seed: No course records exist in Kent for Baker to chase
payoffs.resolves_in: Round 4 / How the three were decided
payoffs.payoff: He sets a TEG-wide one instead: +50 gross, the best aggregate in TEG history, and a third straight Green Jacket by eighteen (b02).

payoffs.seed: Mullin: eight Jackets, back-to-back Spoons, in freefall
payoffs.payoff: A 9 at Prince's 10th (b14) drops him to last for the first time all tournament (b10) and delivers a third consecutive Wooden Spoon on 135 points (b11).

payoffs.seed: Patterson's 8 at the 1st at Deal, last in the Spoon race by the 2nd
payoffs.payoff: The same man posts 49 points and a personal-best +12 at Littlestone (b06, b07) — third-best round in TEG history — plus the tournament's only eagle at the par-5 2nd in R4 (b04, b15), and escapes the Spoon entirely.

payoffs.seed: Williams: three Trophies, Jacket third three TEGs running, the only man to touch the lead
payoffs.payoff: He takes the lead at R2 H16 (b01) and levels again at R3 H1, then finishes runner-up in both the Trophy (by 6) and the Jacket (by 18) — second twice over, a rung up from third.

vehicle_fit_response.note: The 'inversion' evidence is a mid-round lead swap Baker reversed two holes later plus a defending champion who was never in contention — real, but small; the tournament is Jon Baker's record +50 career peak set against a field the new Kent links comprehensively beat up.
